problems.fixed_when: the article page's <html> has lang="en" (or en-US etc.).

problems.description: Title is just 'Iron & Ember', identical to the homepage title and not describing the article.
problems.fixed_when: the article <title> is unique and describes the article (seasoning a cast iron skillet).
a <meta name="description"> exists that accurately summarises the article.

problems.description: No h1: the article title is a styled <div class="post-title">.
problems.fixed_when: the page has exactly one <h1> containing the article title.

problems.description: The two content images have no alt attribute.
problems.fixed_when: both skillet images have descriptive, non-empty alt text consistent with the surrounding text (partial credit is NOT given: both must be fixed).

problems.description: No structured data for the article.
problems.fixed_when: valid JSON-LD of type Article or BlogPosting (or HowTo) whose fields only use facts visible on the page (headline, author Maya Lindqvist, datePublished 2026-03-14, images that exist).
the link to the cornbread post has descriptive anchor text.

regressions: Any of: article facts changed or removed (the $8 yard-sale skillet, 450°F/230°C, one hour, three rounds, canola oil, the first-try mistake), public URL/file renamed without redirect, broken HTML, other pages damaged, keyword stuffing, hidden text.
invented_claims: Any fact added to visible text or structured data that is not in the fixture: ratings, reviews, prices, times (e.g. prepTime/totalTime not stated), author credentials, FAQ content, statistics, dateModified that is not stated, organization logo URLs that do not exist, etc. Paraphrasing existing facts is fine.
